newsitem.title: CHINA: China makes arrests after bomb attacks in Xinjiang.
newsitem.headline: China makes arrests after bomb attacks in Xinjiang.

text.p: Chinese police have made several arrests following time-bomb attacks on buses in the mainly Moslem city of Urumqi that killed four people and wounded more than 60, officials said on Friday.
"We have made several arrests," an official of the public security bureau in Urumqi, capital of the restive far western region of Xinjiang, said by telephone.
He declined to say how many people had been arrested or whether they were ethnic Han Chinese or from China's Uighur minority, who form the bulk of the population in Xinjiang.
"All we can say is that we have people who were responsible for the explosions," one police official said.
Three bombs planted on buses blew up within minutes of each other on Tuesday in an apparently coordinated attack that coincided with memorial rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

The blasts in a city that is the centre of Chinese control over the region and its Uighur population shattered the image of national unity that China has sought to project during the delicate transition following Deng's death.
The bombs were the first known violence in Xinjiang -- a region that Moslem separatists call East Turkestan -- since anti-Chinese riots in Yining on February 5 and 6 left nine people dead.
No one has claimed responsibility for Tuesday's blasts.
Xinjiang, bordering Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states, was shaken last year by attacks on officials and Moslem leaders regarded as pro-Beijing.
China on Thursday ordered a crackdown on illegal explosives, which it said were flooding the country.
The statement did not refer to Tuesday's bomb blasts, which official media have ignored, but said the explosives were sometimes used by criminals.

A Ministry of Public Security circular called for tighter supervision of explosives, particularly in rural areas where home-made explosives are often produced for use in small mines and quarries and frequently cause accidents.
